clue.text: Judge saw criminal giving talks

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or bent, so the letters of the word saw are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A judge watches a crook being given a stern lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talks' looks like a noun, but here it is a verb: someone who jaws chatters on at length.
explanation.definitionFit: To jaw is an informal verb for chatting or talking at length, often tediously.

clue.text: Seconds includes Eton mess with seeds

indicators.note: one piece wrapping around another means the outer letters include the inner ones

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second, so two seconds give a pair of them

indicators.note: a mess is a jumbled state, so the letters of Eton are muddled up, with a nod to the pudding Eton mess

explanation.surface: A recipe note: second helpings of the strawberry pudding come with pips in.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton mess is a British dessert of strawberries, cream and broken meringue; here 'mess' is the anagram signal, turning ETON into TONE between the two S's.
explanation.definitionFit: Stones are the hard seeds found in fruits such as cherries, plums and peaches.

clue.text: New Age rock supports metal plants

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: green means new or inexperienced, as in a green recruit
Al is the chemical symbol for the metal aluminium

indicators.note: to rock is to shake, so the letters of age are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Hippie music props up a heavy-metal band, as a pop-culture mash-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Age rock' reads as one musical genre, but it splits three ways: New gives GREEN, and 'rock' shakes AGE into GAE, placed under AL because 'supports' works top to bottom in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Green algae are simple chlorophyll-bearing organisms, traditionally classed as plants, found in ponds and seas.

clue.text: Girl's transport delivered

indicators.note: a speech is delivered when spoken, so the word is said out loud and heard as a name

parts.note: to transport something is to carry it

explanation.surface: A girl's taxi or courier has dropped off its parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' suggests a parcel arriving, but it means spoken, as a speech is delivered: CARRY spoken aloud sounds like the name. The 's is short for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrie is a girl's first name, and also the Stephen King horror film behind this puzzle's theme.

clue.text: Conservative peer noticed tool

parts.note: Peter Hain, a former Labour cabinet minister, sits in the House of Lords as Lord Hain
saw means noticed or spotted

explanation.surface: A Tory member of the Lords spotted a piece of equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' suggests the verb look, especially beside 'noticed', but it is a member of the House of Lords, the UK's upper chamber: Lord Hain.
explanation.definitionFit: A chainsaw is a powered cutting tool with teeth fixed to a moving loop of chain.

clue.text: They rescue sick parrots, bandaging heads

indicators.note: the heads of words are their opening letters, so the first letter of each of the four words is taken

explanation.surface: Kind volunteers save ailing parrots by wrapping their heads in bandages.
explanation.walkthrough: The RSPB is the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds, a large British bird charity, so the whole clue paints what it might do; the letters are entered as one word despite being initials.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun stands for the bird charity, whom the rest of the clue describes caring for injured birds.

clue.text: One releasing those caught in possession?

definitions.text: One releasing those caught in possession?

parts.words: One releasing those caught in possession?
parts.note: sounds like someone freeing people caught with drugs on them, but describes freeing people possessed by demons

explanation.surface: A lenient official lets off people caught holding illegal drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possession' reads as the drugs offence, but it is demonic possession; the person who frees the possessed drives the spirit out.
explanation.definitionFit: An exorcist casts evil spirits out of a person, freeing someone in the grip of a demon.

clue.text: So, today's not the 4th?

indicators.note: the fourth letter of the day's short form is left out

parts.note: the puzzle was published on a Thursday, so today is Thurs, its usual short form

explanation.surface: A confused question about the date: isn't today the fourth of the month?
explanation.walkthrough: 'The 4th' looks like a date, but it is the fourth letter of THURS, the R. The clue relies on the day it appeared in the paper, a Thursday.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus and so are both adverbs meaning therefore or in this way.

clue.text: Art thief: 'Am I not worried by consequences?'

indicators.note: to worry something is to tug or shake it about, as a dog worries a bone, so the letters are shaken into a new order
the word I is not included, so it is taken out of the letters of thief

explanation.surface: An art thief anxiously asks whether the fallout from the heist will catch up with him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Am I not worried' reads as a question, but 'I not' removes I from THIEF, leaving THEF, and 'worried' rearranges ART + THEF + AM.
explanation.definitionFit: The aftermath of an event is its results or the period of effects following it.

clue.text: Team enters hard times over position in league?

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so the assembled letters are read backwards

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: one piece entering another goes inside it

parts.note: T stands for time, so times are Ts
a cricket or football team is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A sports club joins in tough times and ends up in an unwanted league place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enters' puts XI inside H and TS to make HTXIS, and 'over' then turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sixth is a ranking in a league table; the question mark flags that it is just one example of a position.

clue.text: Shakin' Stevens ignoring TV impression

indicators.note: shaking jumbles things up, so the remaining letters are shuffled
ignoring the letters T and V means they are left out of the singer's surname

explanation.surface: Shakin' Stevens, the Welsh rock and roll singer, makes an impression without television's help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignoring' drops T and V from STEVENS, leaving SEENS, which 'Shakin'' rearranges; the singer's first name supplies the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sense of something is a vague feeling or impression of it, as in a sense of unease.

clue.text: Nature's forecasters use brains to obtain current research and development

indicators.note: obtaining something means taking it in, so the rearranged letters hold the other pieces
brains are used, worked over, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current in physics
R and D, or RD, is the usual short form of research and development

explanation.surface: A science funding pitch: put your brains to work on electrical research.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use' is the anagram signal, turning BRAINS into RAINBS; 'to obtain' then places I and RD inside it, between the B and the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainbird is a folk name for birds such as the green woodpecker, whose calls were thought to foretell rain.

clue.text: Loss of money earned over players — 100's missing

indicators.note: the money earned is placed over, covering both sides of, the shortened players

parts.note: a wage is money earned for work

indicators.note: with C missing, that letter is dropped from the word for the players

parts.note: the cast of a play is its players
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A theatre company's accounts: wages paid to actors, with a hundred pounds unaccounted for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing' drops C from CAST, leaving AST, and 'over' wraps WAGE around it, between W and AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wastage is the amount lost through waste, leakage or natural decline.

clue.text: After removing top, change into an enchantress

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, so the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: to switch is to change or swap

explanation.surface: Someone takes off a hat and is transformed into a sorceress, as in a fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removing top' sounds like undressing, but it means the first letter of SWITCH goes, since the top of a down word is its start.
explanation.definitionFit: A witch is a woman believed to practise magic, which is what an enchantress does.

clue.text: Bright sun, next to Mercury, orbits cool pair

indicators.note: the pieces are placed side by side, one after the other

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for sun, as for Sunday

indicators.note: a body that orbits another goes round it, so these letters surround the others

parts.note: Hg is the chemical symbol for the element mercury

indicators.note: a pair is two of the same, so the word for cool is used twice

parts.note: in means cool or fashionable

explanation.surface: Astronomy: the bright sun beside the planet Mercury, around which two bodies circle.
explanation.walkthrough: The astronomical surface hides the abbreviations: sun is S and Mercury is the element's symbol, not the planet; 'orbits' and 'pair' are the container and doubling signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Shining means giving out bright light, so it is a direct synonym for bright.

clue.text: Funny film about old vehicle reversing to happen in seaside resort

indicators.note: one piece goes about another when it surrounds it
funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters of film come out in a strange order
a vehicle reversing goes backwards, so these letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to be is to exist or take place, so it can mean to happen

explanation.surface: A comedy film about an old banger backing into something at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' rearranges FILM into ILFM, and 'about' puts RACO (O and CAR, read backwards for 'reversing') inside it. Ilfracombe is a seaside town in north Devon, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilfracombe is a well-known holiday town on the Devon coast, a classic British seaside resort.

clue.text: Toast and orange squash with afternoon off

indicators.note: to squash something is to crush it out of shape, so the remaining letters are rearranged
taking a letter off means dropping it from the word orange

explanation.surface: An afternoon tea order: buttered toast and an orange squash drink, though the afternoon is cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: Orange squash is a British fruit cordial diluted with water. Here 'squash' is the anagram signal, and 'off' removes A from ORANGE, leaving ORNGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is toast, in slang, is doomed or finished, which is what a goner is.

clue.text: Object of night shift

indicators.note: to shift is to move objects around, so the letters of night change places

explanation.surface: The purpose of working the night shift is questioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Night shift' looks like a work rota, but 'shift' is the anagram signal for NIGHT, and 'Object' is the noun meaning an item.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is any physical item, so it is a general word for an object.

clue.text: Playing tennis, keeping ball on line is rude

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so the rearranged letters contain the others
letters at play move about freely, so the word tennis is rearranged
in a down entry, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: O looks like a ball

explanation.surface: A tennis player who keeps hitting the ball on the line is accused of bad manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' rearranges TENNIS into INSENT, and 'keeping' puts OL between INS and ENT; 'is' only links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent describes boldly rude or disrespectful behaviour, so it is a stronger synonym for rude.

clue.text: Foot as party leader was somewhat untidy

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
untidy means messy, so the remaining letters are put out of order
somewhat means only partly, so the word was loses part of itself, its last letter

explanation.surface: The head of a political party is criticised for being a little scruffy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhat' trims WAS to WA, and 'untidy' turns that to AW, after the P from 'party leader'.
explanation.definitionFit: A paw is the foot of an animal such as a cat or dog.

clue.text: Plans for launches

definitions.meaning: schemes or planned pieces of work, as nouns
sends forth or throws, as a verb, as when a missile is fired

explanation.surface: Planning schemes that are about to be launched.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means planned undertakings; the verb means throws or fires forward, so both senses share one spelling.

clue.text: Pleasure holding books, retiring to bed

indicators.note: one piece holding another wraps around it

parts.note: fun is pleasure or enjoyment

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the letters of the books are read backwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a good read before heading to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' suggests going to bed, but it turns OT round to TO, which 'holding' puts inside FUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A futon is a Japanese-style padded mattress, used as a bed that can be rolled or folded away.

clue.text: Succeeded in developing theory about the womb

indicators.note: one piece is put in the middle of another
something developing changes shape, so the letters of theory are reformed

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone succeeds in developing a scientific theory about pregnancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Developing' rearranges THEORY, and 'in' puts S inside it, between HY and TERO.
explanation.definitionFit: The combining form hystero- relates to the uterus, as in hysterotomy, from Greek hystera.

clue.text: Promotion involves salary increase for flatterer

indicators.note: one piece involving another surrounds it

parts.note: PR, public relations, is promotion of a company or product
a raise is an increase in pay

explanation.surface: Getting promoted at work comes with a bump in pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promotion' suggests a job step up, but it means publicity; 'involves' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A praiser speaks well of someone, and a flatterer is one who praises excessively.

clue.text: At home I sleep, rising to make a sandwich

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from the bottom up, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: Someone naps at home, then gets up to fix a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' sounds like getting out of bed, but it reverses IN + I + NAP, reading up the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A panini is a grilled Italian-style sandwich made with ciabatta or similar bread.

clue.text: Hilarious person in Sunday best

parts.note: the cream is the best part, as in the cream of the crop

explanation.surface: A funny guest turns up dressed in their finest clothes for church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sunday best' reads as smart clothes, but it splits into S and CREAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A scream is informal for someone extremely funny, as in 'she's a scream'.

clue.text: He let in English nationalist for celebration

indicators.note: the word for let is put in the middle of he

parts.note: to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A man welcomed an English nationalist to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let in' looks like one phrase meaning admit, but 'in' is the container signal acting on the synonym for 'let'.
explanation.definitionFit: Halloween, on 31 October, is a festival marked with costumes and trick-or-treating, an annual celebration.

clue.text: Man will cause commotion …

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
'll is the contracted form of will

explanation.surface: A man will kick up a fuss, the clue running on into the next one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man will' reads as HE'LL with the apostrophe dropped; 'cause' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell, as in 'all hell broke loose', means noisy uproar or chaos.

clue.text: … with 'female only' sign

parts.note: a space for women only has nil men in it, so the words are read as O (zero) beside MEN

explanation.surface: Continuing from the last clue, a man makes a fuss about a women-only sign on a door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female only' means there are no men, which is written as O (zero) followed by MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent or sign of something to come.

clue.text: Monsters? Turn back — no time to wait!

indicators.note: back means backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in board games

indicators.note: no means without, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: to rest is to stay or wait

explanation.surface: Fleeing monsters, someone shouts to turn around at once and not linger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn back' reads as an order to retreat, but 'back' reverses GO to OG; 'no time' takes T from REST, leaving RES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are man-eating giants of folklore, a classic kind of monster.

clue.text: Waves one off from plane

indicators.note: taking the word for one off means removing those letters

parts.note: a plane is a flat surface
an ace is a one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Someone waves goodbye as a single passenger gets off an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' suggests an aircraft, but it is a flat surface; ACE, the one in cards, comes off the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Surf is the mass of breaking waves and foam on a shore.

clue.text: Pierce Brosnan finally wears tie

indicators.note: something worn is held within, so the lace goes around the letter

parts.note: a lace is a tie, as for a shoe

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the word, so its last letter is used

explanation.surface: The actor Pierce Brosnan finally puts on a necktie, as a smart James Bond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pierce Brosnan' looks like one name, but the first name is the definition, as a verb; 'wears' puts N inside LACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lance is to pierce or cut open, as a surgeon does with a boil.

clue.text: Fake Tory in Labour? Not our former PM

indicators.note: something fake is concocted or made up, so the letters are recombined
with our not included, those letters are dropped from the party name

explanation.surface: A disgruntled Labour member grumbles about a Tory masquerading in their party, disowning a former leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not our' takes OUR out of LABOUR, leaving LAB; 'Fake' rearranges TORY + IN + LAB. Tony Blair led Labour and was UK Prime Minister 1997-2007, often accused by critics of being Tory-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair was the UK Prime Minister from 1997 to 2007, so he is a former head of government.
